artifacts.summary: All 7 plan phases completed: fetch_path1 temp-file accumulator with loud failure and Total-Results-driven pagination, authoritative itemType filter, content-keyed shrink guard with --allow-shrink, corrected fetch_path3 itemTypeID exclusion, 11-case offline regression suite, and doc updates.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed the silent-truncation data-loss defect in zotero-generate-export.sh's Path 1 by rewriting fetch_path1() with a temp-file accumulator, Total-Results-driven pagination, and loud failure with no partial write; added a content-keyed shrink guard, corrected fetch_path3's itemTypeID exclusion set, and delivered an 11-case offline regression suite plus documentation updates.

memory_candidates.content: For a PATH-shadowing test stub (curl-stub.sh style) that needs to locate sibling fixture/generator files, resolve its own directory via `readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"` rather than plain `dirname(BASH_SOURCE)`. Callers commonly install the stub as `curl` in a scratch PATH dir via either `cp` or `ln -s`; only the symlink form resolves back to the real directory (and its siblings) through readlink -f. Document both install forms and add an explicit env-var override for callers that must `cp`.

Linux's MAX_ARG_STRLEN (128KiB per single argv argument, independent of the larger ARG_MAX) silently kills a `jq --argjson` accumulation loop once the accumulated value crosses that size -- and a trailing `2>/dev/null || echo "$prior_value"` fallback swallows the failure entirely, making the script exit 0 with a silently truncated result. The general-purpose fix: never pass a growing value via a single argv argument; write each unit to its own temp file and combine once via `jq -s 'add'` (or `jq -s` equivalent) at the end, and delete any error-swallowing fallback so a combine failure aborts loudly instead of returning a stale/partial value as success.

Zotero sqlite/API itemTypeID values are not stable identifiers -- they can differ across installations/versions, so hardcoding a numeric itemTypeID exclusion/inclusion set (e.g. `NOT IN (1, 3, 28)`) can silently mean the wrong types on a different install with zero error signal. Resolve such filters by TYPE NAME via a subquery/join against the type-name table (e.g. `itemTypes.typeName`) instead. Also note: Zotero's CSL-JSON export maps itemType `attachment` to CSL type `document` (never `"attachment"`), so a CSL `.type`-based exclusion filter for attachments/notes is a no-op; the authoritative type must come from the raw (non-CSL) API/DB response, cross-referenced by item key.
